label: Radicalized Beauvoir's 'becomes a woman' into performative gender theory
description: Judith Butler took Beauvoir's thesis that 'one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman' as the point of departure for Gender Trouble, stripping away residual Cartesian voluntarism to argue that both sex and gender are discursively produced.
dialecticalTension: Moves from existentialist project of becoming to Foucauldian-Derridean iterative performativity.
historicalContext: Opening argument of Gender Trouble (1990) and 'Sex and Gender in Simone de Beauvoir's Second Sex' (1986).

label: Adapted Foucauldian productive power to explain regulatory sex/gender norms
description: Drawing on Foucault's History of Sexuality, Butler argued that juridical power does not merely repress a pre-existing sexed subject, but productively materializes the very subject it claims to represent.
dialecticalTension: Explains how subversion remains possible from within productive disciplinary norms.
historicalContext: Core post-structuralist architecture of Gender Trouble (1990) and Bodies That Matter (1993).

label: Supplied iterability and citationality for performative norm subversion
description: Butler adapted Derrida's reading of Austin's speech acts ('Signature Event Context') to argue that gender operates via citational repetition, whose inherent iterability opens space for parodic misfire and resignification.
dialecticalTension: Turns linguistic iterability into a theory of embodied political and sexual agency.
historicalContext: Elaborated in Bodies That Matter (1993) and Excitable Speech (1997).

label: Synthesized Hegelian recognition and desire with post-structuralist ethics
description: Starting from her dissertation Subjects of Desire (1987) through Giving an Account of Oneself (2005), Butler reworked Hegel's master-slave dialectic of recognition to theorize mutual vulnerability and ethical responsibility.
dialecticalTension: Reconciles Hegelian relational recognition with Foucauldian opacity of the subject.
historicalContext: Spans Butler's early Hegelian scholarship and later ethical turn.

citations.author: Judith Butler
citations.work: Subjects of Desire: Hegelian Reflections in Twentieth-Century France

label: Formulated the philosophical theory of gender performativity
description: Butler coined and systematized gender performativity as the compulsory repetition of gendered norms that produces the illusion of an abiding internal gender core.
dialecticalTension: Dissolves biological-determinist and expressive models of identity.

label: Provoked Ljubljana School psychoanalytic critique of pure discursive performativity
description: Alenka Zupančič engaged Butler's performative constructivism in What Is Sex? (2017), arguing from Lacanian psychoanalysis that sexual difference is not merely a discursive norm, but an ontological Real/impasse within signification itself.
dialecticalTension: Pits post-structuralist discursive performativity against Lacanian ontology of the non-discursive Real.
historicalContext: Contemporary debate between American queer theory and Ljubljana School psychoanalysis.
